Let's obviously assume that <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="d_k" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-msub data-latex="d_k"><mjx-mi data-latex="d"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D451">𝑑</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-script style="vertical-align: -0.15em;"><mjx-mi size="s" data-latex="k"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D458">𝑘</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-script></mjx-msub></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="d_k"><msub data-latex="d_k"><mi data-latex="d">d</mi><mi data-latex="k">k</mi></msub></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> has been precomputed.</p>
<p>Consider the following pseudo-code that does this:</p>
<pre class="hljs"><code>p = nodes on the path from 1 to n
sat = true

for i from 1 to n:
    v = p[i]
    for j from 1 to i:
        u = p[j]
        if dk[u] + dk[v] <= dis_P(u, v):
            sat = false
</code></pre>
<p>This works in <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="O(n^2)" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="O"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D442">𝑂</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex="("><mjx-c class="mjx-c28">(</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-msup data-latex="n^2"><mjx-mi data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-script style="vertical-align: 0.363em;"><mjx-mn size="s" data-latex="2"><mjx-c class="mjx-c32">2</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-script></mjx-msup><mjx-mo data-latex=")"><mjx-c class="mjx-c29">)</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="O(n^2)"><mi data-latex="O">O</mi><mo data-latex="(" stretchy="false">(</mo><msup data-latex="n^2"><mi data-latex="n">n</mi><mn data-latex="2">2</mn></msup><mo data-latex=")" stretchy="false">)</mo></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> (forget about the precomputation for now), but can we do better? We realize that the distance function <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="\text{dis}_P(u, v)" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-msub data-latex="\text{dis}_P"><mjx-mtext data-latex="\text{dis}"><mjx-c class="mjx-c64" noic="true" style="padding-top: 0.694em;">d</mjx-c><mjx-c class="mjx-c69" noic="true" style="padding-top: 0.694em;">i</mjx-c><mjx-c class="mjx-c73" style="padding-top: 0.694em;">s</mjx-c></mjx-mtext><mjx-script style="vertical-align: -0.15em;"><mjx-mi size="s" data-latex="P"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D443">𝑃</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-script></mjx-msub><mjx-mo data-latex="("><mjx-c class="mjx-c28">(</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mi data-latex="u"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D462">𝑢</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex=","><mjx-c class="mjx-c2C">,</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mi space="2" data-latex="v"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D463">𝑣</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex=")"><mjx-c class="mjx-c29">)</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="\text{dis}_P(u, v)"><msub data-latex="\text{dis}_P"><mtext data-latex="\text{dis}">dis</mtext><mi data-latex="P">P</mi></msub><mo data-latex="(" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi data-latex="u">u</mi><mo data-latex=",">,</mo><mi data-latex="v">v</mi><mo data-latex=")" stretchy="false">)</mo></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> has a rather "continuous" nature, and we can exploit this to do something similar to kadane's algorithm (just maintain the value of the extreme suffix).</p>
<p>This leads to the following <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="O(n)" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="O"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D442">𝑂</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex="("><mjx-c class="mjx-c28">(</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mi data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex=")"><mjx-c class="mjx-c29">)</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="O(n)"><mi data-latex="O">O</mi><mo data-latex="(" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi data-latex="n">n</mi><mo data-latex=")" stretchy="false">)</mo></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> solution:</p>
<pre class="hljs"><code>p = nodes on the path from 1 to n
sat = true
worst_suffix = -dk[p[1]]

for i from 2 to n:
    v = p[i]
    worst_suffix = max(worst_suffix + dis_P(p[i - 1], v), -dk[v])
    if dk[v] <= worst_suffix:
        sat = false
</code></pre>
<p>Alright, let's now consider doing this for arbitrary paths in a general graph.</p>
<p>We will try to incrementally build good paths from node <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="1" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mn data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="1"><mn data-latex="1">1</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> that have the potential to satisfy <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="1" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mn data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="1"><mn data-latex="1">1</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>. What properties must such a potential path from <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="1" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mn data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="1"><mn data-latex="1">1</mn></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> to <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="u" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="u"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D462">𝑢</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="u"><mi data-latex="u">u</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> satisfy?</p>
<ul>
<li>It must not contain <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="k" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="k"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D458">𝑘</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="k"><mi data-latex="k">k</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>.</li>
<li><mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="(1)" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mo data-latex="("><mjx-c class="mjx-c28">(</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mn data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn><mjx-mo data-latex=")"><mjx-c class="mjx-c29">)</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="(1)"><mo data-latex="(" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn data-latex="1">1</mn><mo data-latex=")" stretchy="false">)</mo></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> must obviously be satisfied for <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="g, h" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="g"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D454">𝑔</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex=","><mjx-c class="mjx-c2C">,</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mi space="2" data-latex="h"><mjx-c class="mjx-c210E">ℎ</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="g, h"><mi data-latex="g">g</mi><mo data-latex=",">,</mo><mi data-latex="h">h</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> on this prefix path.</li>
<li>In addition, note that as long as <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="(1)" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mo data-latex="("><mjx-c class="mjx-c28">(</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mn data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn><mjx-mo data-latex=")"><mjx-c class="mjx-c29">)</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="(1)"><mo data-latex="(" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn data-latex="1">1</mn><mo data-latex=")" stretchy="false">)</mo></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> is satisfied on this prefix, the only thing that will affect <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="(1)" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mo data-latex="("><mjx-c class="mjx-c28">(</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mn data-latex="1"><mjx-c class="mjx-c31">1</mjx-c></mjx-mn><mjx-mo data-latex=")"><mjx-c class="mjx-c29">)</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="(1)"><mo data-latex="(" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn data-latex="1">1</mn><mo data-latex=")" stretchy="false">)</mo></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> as we further extend this path is the analogous value of <code>worst_suffix</code> until now. It's easy to see that we should aim to minimise this value.</li>
</ul>
<p>This trivially leads to the following <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="O(n\cdot m)" breakable="true" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="O"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D442">𝑂</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex="("><mjx-c class="mjx-c28">(</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mi data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-break size="3"> </mjx-break><mjx-mo data-latex="\cdot"><mjx-c class="mjx-c22C5">⋅</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mi space="3" data-latex="m"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45A">𝑚</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex=")"><mjx-c class="mjx-c29">)</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="O(n\cdot m)"><mi data-latex="O">O</mi><mo data-latex="(" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi data-latex="n">n</mi><mo data-latex="\cdot">⋅</mo><mi data-latex="m">m</mi><mo data-latex=")" stretchy="false">)</mo></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> algorithm (just have <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="n" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="n"><mi data-latex="n">n</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container> rounds (max number of nodes in <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="P" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="P"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D443">𝑃</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="P"><mi data-latex="P">P</mi></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>) where you try to transition across every edge).</p>
<pre class="hljs"><code>precompute dk using djikstras

opt[n]

opt[1] = -dk[1]
for u from 2 to n:
    opt[u] = inf

for round from 1 to n:
    nopt = opt
    for u from 1 to n:
        for [v, l, r] in adj[u]:
            if (u != k and v != k and dk[v] > opt[u] + l)
                nopt[v] = min(nopt[v], max(-dk[v], opt[u] + l))
    opt = nopt

if opt[n] != inf:
    valid assignment exists
</code></pre>
<p>To optimize this to <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="CHTML" overflow="overflow" style="font-size: 113.1%; position: relative;"><mjx-math data-latex="O((n + m) \log{n})" breakable="true" class="NCM-N" aria-hidden="true"><mjx-mi data-latex="O"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D442">𝑂</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex="("><mjx-c class="mjx-c28">(</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mo data-latex="("><mjx-c class="mjx-c28">(</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mi data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-break size="3"> </mjx-break><mjx-mo data-latex="+"><mjx-c class="mjx-c2B">+</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mi space="3" data-latex="m"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45A">𝑚</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo data-latex=")"><mjx-c class="mjx-c29">)</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-mi space="2" data-latex="\log"><mjx-c class="mjx-c6C" noic="true" style="padding-top: 0.694em;">l</mjx-c><mjx-c class="mjx-c6F" noic="true" style="padding-top: 0.694em;">o</mjx-c><mjx-c class="mjx-c67" style="padding-top: 0.694em;">g</mjx-c></mjx-mi><mjx-mo><mjx-c class="mjx-c2061">⁡</mjx-c></mjx-mo><mjx-TeXAtom space="2" data-latex="{n}" texclass="ORD"><mjx-mi data-latex="n"><mjx-c class="mjx-c1D45B">𝑛</mjx-c></mjx-mi></mjx-TeXAtom><mjx-mo data-latex=")"><mjx-c class="mjx-c29">)</mjx-c></mjx-mo></mjx-math><mjx-assistive-mml unselectable="on" display="inline"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" data-latex="O((n + m) \log{n})"><mi data-latex="O">O</mi><mo data-latex="(" stretchy="false">(</mo><mo data-latex="(" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi data-latex="n">n</mi><mo data-latex="+">+</mo><mi data-latex="m">m</mi><mo data-latex=")" stretchy="false">)</mo><mi data-latex="\log">log</mi><mo data-mjx-texclass="NONE">⁡</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD" data-latex="{n}"><mi data-latex="n">n</mi></mrow><mo data-latex=")" stretchy="false">)</mo></math></mjx-assistive-mml></mjx-container>, we can simply observe that we can use a Djikstra's like approach here due to the monotonic nature of the transitions (due to strictly positive edge weights).</p>
